about: GEOMETRY equations only: the 'hidden' ones that are not on the exam paper (areas, perimeters, effective dimensions, drainage path, pressure-diagram areas). Real equations (the f logo) are given on the paper, so they are not written on the cards. Keys are notation ids. "front" replaces the meaning on the card front where the notation sheet's wording already contains the equation.

equations.n003:
B′ = B − 2ex    L′ = L − 2ey
effective width and length: only the part of the base centred on the load carries it
equations.n009:
A = πR² = πB²/4   (B = 2R)
area of a circular loaded area; circumference 2πR
equations.n007:
z = (depth to the top of the layer) + H/2
depth of the middle of a layer, where σ′0 and Δσ are taken
equations.n010:
Hbelow base = Hlayer − Df
thickness of a layer beneath the footing is measured from the foundation level, not the ground surface
equations.n011:
m = b/z    n = l/z
sides of the rectangle divided by the depth, for the influence chart
equations.n072:
m = b/z    n = l/z
sides of the rectangle divided by the depth, for the influence chart
equations.n012:
e = M/V
eccentricity of the load: moment about the centre of the base over the vertical load; then B′ = B − 2e
equations.n015: strip: A = B (per metre)   square: A = B²   rectangle: A = BL   circle: A = πB²/4
equations.n036:
ΔH/H = Δe/(1 + e0)  ⇒  H ∝ (1 + e)
the solids height is constant, so thickness is proportional to 1 + e
equations.n100:
As = πDL   (square pile: 4DL)
shaft area: perimeter × embedded length
equations.n101:
Ab = πD²/4 = π(D/2)²
base area of a circular pile
equations.n097:
W = Vpγp − Uwater ≈ Ab·h·γs = poAb
pile volume Vp = AbL; the weight is taken equal to the soil it replaced
equations.n106:
po = γs·h
overburden pressure at the level of the base (γ′ below the water table)
equations.n133:
B = (nrow − 1)S + D    W = (ncol − 1)S + D
block size from the pile spacing S and diameter D; perimeter 2(B + W), base area B·W
equations.n161:
Dg = 2R + D
circular group: ring radius R to the pile centres, plus one diameter
equations.n162:
Dg = 2R + D
circular group: ring radius R to the pile centres, plus one diameter
equations.n145:
RA = Anet/Agross = (D² − d²)/D² (hollow)   RA = 1 (solid)
area ratio: net area of pile material over gross area
equations.n169:
Hdr = H/2 (drained top and bottom)   Hdr = H (one face)
longest drainage path
equations.n078: d = H/2 (double drainage)   d = H (single drainage)
equations.n178:
triangle: P = ½pH, acts H/3 above the base   rectangle: P = pH, acts H/2   trapezoid: P = ½(p1 + p2)H
thrust = area of the pressure diagram; its line of action = centroid of that area

front.n078: drainage path length (double or single drainage)
front.n097: self-weight of a pile, net of the water it displaces
front.n100: area of the pile shaft in contact with the soil
front.n101: area of the base of a circular pile
front.n106: overburden pressure at the level of the pile base
front.n145: area ratio of a pile (net area of material over gross area)
front.n161: ring radius of a circular pile group
front.n169: longest drainage path of a clay layer
front.n178: total active / passive force per metre length of wall
